events.title: U.S. Dollar Adopted as Currency
events.description: The Continental Congress resolved that the monetary unit of the United States would be the dollar, using a decimal system for coinage.
events.significance: Established the foundation of the American monetary system, moving away from British pounds and Spanish coinage toward a decimal-based national currency.

events.title: Louis Pasteur Tests Rabies Vaccine
events.description: Louis Pasteur administered the first rabies vaccine to nine-year-old Joseph Meister, who had been bitten by a rabid dog.
events.significance: Marked a milestone in immunology and vaccine development, demonstrating that vaccines could prevent disease after exposure and paving the way for modern vaccination.

events.title: Death of Henry II of England
events.description: Henry II, the first Plantagenet king of England, died at Chinon Castle in France, after a reign of 35 years, following a rebellion by his sons Richard and John.
events.significance: His death led to the accession of Richard the Lionheart and ended the reign that built the Angevin Empire and developed English common law.

events.title: Execution of Sir Thomas More
events.description: Sir Thomas More, former Lord Chancellor of England, was beheaded for refusing to accept Henry VIII as Supreme Head of the Church of England.
events.significance: More's execution became a lasting symbol of conscience against state power; he was later canonized as a saint by the Catholic Church.

events.title: Birth of the Dalai Lama's Birthday Observed
events.description: Tenzin Gyatso, the 14th Dalai Lama, was born on July 6, 1935, in Taktser, Tibet, and was later recognized as the reincarnation of his predecessor.
events.significance: As spiritual and political leader of Tibet, he won the 1989 Nobel Peace Prize and became a global advocate for nonviolence and Tibetan autonomy.
